doc.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017

title: Orlando's musical climate and contracting
summary: He recalls Orlando's busy music scene and contracting orchestras for Ray Charles and the Moody Blues.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Because there’s no, there’s no comp — there’s no more downtown this and downtown that. Like at Rosie O’Grady’s, when Rosie O’Grady’s was running in downtown Orlando, and when Disney was cranking with all their bands and stuff, I mean the musical climate in this town was un-freaking-believable. I mean and I was doing some contracting then where I’d, we’d do orchestral things for Ray Charles and we did a dozen shows with Ray. But you could get on the phone and come up with a band. I’ve put together a 53-piece orchestra to back up the Moody Blues. And you can get them. They’re in town. You know, 36 strings. And the first thing we ever did with them we had 36 strings and two percussionists and two bass viols, and a full woodwind section you know with oboes and English horns and flutes. And then the Moody Blues, who were great guys by the way, from England, we had a lot of common friends over there. Then a sweetener track with four or five things on it and then two or three more musicians who backed them up. I mean all this network of stuff, and I’m thinking to myself, in my inexperience, then I said, “This is going to suck. It’s going to be the worst mess.” It was unbelievably great. I mean the conductor was good. But I mean that was my entrée into doing that.

And I did quite a few of those things. We did a couple of Broadway show things and a lot of things for Ray which was fun. I played in those you know. But over the period of years, when Disney stopped doing all their mega-musical things, it’s too bad. I mean Walt’s idea was a lot of live music but I think, and this is very basic, I think Disney discovered that since the entire continent of South America is going to empty on Orlando every year, they’ve got people coming from Brazil and Argentina.
